LM Studio has integrated Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model into its AI agent platform Bionic, bringing multimodal input capabilities, a 1 million token context window, and pricing significantly lower than GLM-5.2. Details below.

LM Studio swiftly adds GLM-5.3-Flash to Bionic

Since its initial launch in mid-July, LM Studio has continuously expanded the models and features available on its Bionic platform. Bionic is an agentic task platform designed for Mac and Windows, covering work such as coding, research, and handling documents and files.

LM Studio Bionic can use locally run models or cloud-hosted models on US servers, with the latter protected by a strict zero data retention policy.

Shortly after LM Studio Bionic launched, the company added support for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3. Today, the company officially launched cloud support for Z.ai's new model GLM-5.3-Flash, noting its running cost is up to 10 times lower than GLM-5.2.

LM Studio's announcement came just hours after the official release of GLM-5.3-Flash. The model had earlier attracted considerable attention while being tested anonymously under the codename "Ox Alpha" on OpenCode and OpenRouter.

GLM-5.3-Flash is a 320 billion parameter mixture of experts model that activates 18 billion parameters per inference. It supports image and text input and has a 1 million token context window.

In the benchmarks highlighted by Z.ai, GLM-5.3-Flash outperforms GLM-5.2, with overall performance broadly on par with frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek.
